title: Senate to pass the 64-page UAP disclosure bill again

tellings.quote: they're going to they're going to the Senate is going to pass the the 64page bill again

SA 3111. Mr. SCHUMER (for himself, Mr. Rounds, and Mrs. Gillibrand) submitted an amendment intended to be proposed by him to the bill S. 2296, to authorize appropriations for fiscal year 2026 for military activities of the Department of Defense, for military construction, and for defense activities of the Department of Energy, to prescribe military personnel strengths for such fiscal year, and for other purposes; which was ordered to lie on the table; as follows:
This division may be cited as the ``Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2025'' or the ``UAP Disclosure Act of 2025''.

plain: The claim is that the Senate was set to pass again a 64-page bill forcing the government to disclose what it knows about UAP, the official term for UFOs. The lawyer Dan Sheehan, who says he has been part of the effort, tells Michels that "the Senate is going to pass the 64page bill again", naming Senators Mike Rounds, Chuck Schumer and Marco Rubio and Congressman Dan Crenshaw. The bill he means first appeared as the UAP Disclosure Act, an amendment by Schumer and Rounds to the annual defence authorization bill, dated July 13, 2023. The Congressional Record of July 29, 2025 shows it again: amendment SA 3111, which Schumer "submitted" for himself, Rounds and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand to S. 2296, the Senate's defence bill for fiscal year 2026, "which was ordered to lie on the table". The text says it "may be cited as the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2025". That page records the bill being brought back as a submitted amendment; Sheehan's forecast that the Senate would pass it goes a step beyond what it records. If he is right, Congress is pushing to make UFO secrets public by law.

The Record of that day shows the bill brought back to the Senate as a submitted amendment; the teller's forecast that the Senate would pass it goes a step beyond what this page records.
